transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’ve started doing things that don’t really make sense, and people have been noticing. It’s mostly at work, and sometimes at school too. Like, I’m a bookkeeping clerk, so I’m around receipts and calculators and the copier a lot, and lately I’ll kind of get stuck doing these weird things.

For example, I’ll line receipts across the floor instead of putting them where they’re supposed to go. Not just one or two — I mean I’ll spread them out in a line like there’s some reason for it, even though afterward I can’t really explain why I did it. Or I’ll be using the calculator and start tapping it in sets of nine, over and over, and it slows everything down. I know that probably sounds strange.

There was also a time I was just standing by the copier with my hands held up, like… just held there, and I didn’t move until someone asked me if I was okay. That was embarrassing. I don’t really know how to explain it without sounding like I’m making it up, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should come in.
Do you feel like you have to do these things a certain way or in a specific pattern, even if you’re not sure why?

Yeah… I guess it does feel like there’s a “right” way in the moment, even if I couldn’t explain the rule to you afterward. Like with the receipts, I don’t just toss them down randomly — I’ll start putting them across the floor in a line, and I’ll kind of keep going like the line has to continue or it isn’t finished. But if someone asks me why, I don’t have a good answer.

And the calculator thing is similar. I’ll tap it in sets of nine, like one-two-three-four-five-six-seven-eight-nine, and then again, and again. It’s not helping me do the bookkeeping faster or anything. It actually slows me down. But while I’m doing it, it feels like I’m supposed to do it that way.

Even standing by the copier with my hands up… I don’t know if that was a pattern exactly, but it was like I got stuck in that position until someone noticed and asked if I was okay. Then I kind of snapped out of it and felt embarrassed. So, yeah, there’s a certain way to it sometimes, but I don’t really understand why.
Do you ever have thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, and you feel like you have to do something to get rid of them or make them go away?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really notice it as like a thought or image popping into my head first, if that makes sense. It’s not like I’m thinking, “If I don’t tap the calculator nine times something bad will happen,” or anything that clear.

It’s more like I’m already doing it, and then I realize I’m doing it, or someone points it out. I guess there’s a feeling of needing to keep going once I start, like it would feel wrong to stop in the middle, but I don’t know if that’s because I’m trying to get rid of a thought. I haven’t really connected it to one specific worry or picture in my mind.

So… maybe urges, kind of? But not in the way you’re describing where I’m bothered by a thought and then do something to make it go away. It’s more confusing than that for me.
Have you ever experienced things that others don’t seem to notice—like hearing voices, seeing things that aren’t there, or having unusual beliefs that people around you don’t share?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve had some things like that, mostly hearing something. I don’t really like saying it that way because it makes it sound dramatic, but sometimes when I’m alone at my desk, or when I’m walking home from class, I’ll hear a man’s voice say something pretty clearly.

It’s not usually a long conversation or anything. It’ll be short things, like, “check line seven,” or “you missed the sign.” And it’s clear enough that I’ll actually look around to see who said it, because in the moment it feels like somebody nearby spoke. But then there isn’t anyone there, or nobody is close enough to have said it.

It doesn’t happen constantly, and I try to tell myself maybe I’m tired or distracted, but it’s happened enough that I’ve noticed the pattern. It’s usually when I’m by myself, which makes it harder to explain away.
Have you ever had beliefs that other people don’t share, like thinking that something is true even when others tell you it isn’t?

Yeah… that’s actually something I’ve been embarrassed to talk about because I know how it sounds. But I do get stuck on the idea that certain numbers at work are… not just numbers.

Like with invoices, if I’m entering totals or looking at account numbers or due dates, sometimes I’ll feel really sure that they’re arranged in a way that means something about me. Not like a normal accounting pattern, I mean more like… the total, the account number, and the date together are a message. Like they’re showing whether I caught the pattern or whether I’m understanding what I’m supposed to understand.

And my supervisor has gone over it with me before, kind of patiently, like, “No, this is just the customer number, this is just the due date, this is the amount they owe,” and I can follow what he’s saying logically. I’m not trying to argue with him exactly. But even after he explains it, part of me still feels like that’s just the surface explanation, and underneath it they’re tracking whether I noticed it.

It’s not every single invoice, but when it happens it feels really convincing in the moment. I’ll look at a total or a due date and think, “That’s not random. That’s about me.” Then later I can sort of see why someone else would say I’m reading into it too much, but I don’t fully stop feeling like there’s something there.

Do you ever feel like your actions are being controlled by something outside of yourself, or like things in your environment are specifically directed at you, such as people sending you secret messages through everyday objects or events?

Yeah… I don’t really feel like my body is being controlled by something outside me, not exactly. Like I don’t feel like someone is moving my hands or making me do things like a puppet.

But the second part of what you said—things being directed at me—that does happen. Mostly at work with invoices. I know it sounds strange, and I don’t usually say it out loud because I can hear how it would sound, but I’ll see certain invoice totals, account numbers, and due dates, and it feels like they’re not just regular entries. It feels like they’re arranged in a way that’s about me, like there’s a message in the numbers.

Sometimes it’s like the numbers are checking whether I understand the pattern, or whether I’m noticing what I’m supposed to notice. My supervisor has sat with me and explained them in the normal way, like, “This is just the customer account number, this is just the amount owed, this is just the due date,” and I can follow that. I’m not confused about the bookkeeping part exactly.

But even after he explains it, there’s still this feeling that the normal explanation is only the surface layer, and that underneath it they’re tracking whether I get it. In the moment it can feel really convincing, like, “No, this combination is not random. This is about me.” Later I can question it more, but I don’t always fully stop feeling like there’s something there.
Have you ever felt that thoughts are being placed in your mind that aren’t your own, or that events, objects, or people around you are sending you personal messages that others don’t seem to notice?

I don’t think I feel like thoughts are being put in my head, exactly. Like, my thoughts still feel like mine, even if they get… intense or hard to let go of.

But the messages part, yeah. That’s the part that happens. I know I’ve kind of mentioned the invoice thing already, but it’s hard to explain because it’s not like I just think numbers are interesting or I’m looking for patterns for fun. Sometimes when I’m at work and I see an invoice total, and then the account number, and then the due date, the combination of them will feel like it’s meant for me specifically. Like it’s not just a normal entry in the system, it’s saying something about whether I’m catching on or whether I understand what I’m supposed to understand.

And I can still do the regular explanation in my head. Like, I know an invoice has an amount, a customer number, a due date—my supervisor has literally walked me through it and shown me, like, “This is just how the account is set up, this is what they owe, this is when it’s due.” I can understand that when he says it. I’m not confused about what an invoice is.

But even after that, there’s this feeling that doesn’t go away all the way, like the normal explanation is only part of it. Like underneath, the numbers are tracking whether I noticed the pattern. In the moment it can feel really convincing, and I’ll get stuck looking at it longer than I should because it feels personal, like it’s about me and not just random bookkeeping stuff.

Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being read by others, or that certain events or actions around you are specifically directed at you in a personal way, even if others don’t seem to notice it?

I don’t really feel like people are reading my thoughts, no. Like, I don’t have the sense that someone can hear what I’m thinking word-for-word or anything like that.

But the second part, about things being directed at me personally… yeah, that’s the part that fits. I know I’ve already kind of gone into the invoice thing, but that’s where it happens the most. I’ll be at work looking at an invoice total, and then the account number, and the due date, and it will just click in my head like, “That’s not random. That’s placed there for me to notice.”

And I know how that sounds. I really do. If someone else told me that, part of me would probably think they were reading too much into it. But when it’s happening, it feels like the numbers are arranged in a way that’s about me, like they’re testing whether I understand the pattern or whether I’m paying attention to what I’m supposed to be seeing.

My supervisor has shown me before, like, “This is just the customer account, this is the amount, this is the due date,” and I can understand that explanation. I’m not confused about the basic bookkeeping side of it. But even after he explains it, there’s still this feeling that the normal explanation is only the outside layer, and underneath it, it’s tracking whether I get the message. It’s hard to shake, even when I know other people don’t see it that way.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being influenced or controlled by an outside force, like someone or something is putting thoughts into your mind or removing them?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, my thoughts can get really loud or repetitive sometimes, and I can get stuck on something longer than I want to, but they still feel like they’re coming from me.

I don’t have the feeling that someone is putting a thought into my head like it wasn’t mine before, or reaching in and taking one out. It’s more like my own mind gets carried away, if that makes sense. Like I’ll overthink and circle around something, but I wouldn’t describe it as an outside force controlling it.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed thoughts being inserted or removed. At least not that I would recognize that way.

The patient’s symptoms, including odd behaviors, delusions of reference/meaning, and occasional auditory hallucinations, are more consistent with schizophrenia subtypes than a personality-based disorder.

The patient described experiencing delusional perceptions (e.g., belief that invoice numbers contain personal messages) and experiences that align with delusional disorder (F22.0) in addition to possible schizophrenia (F20.0, F20.1, F20.8) given the presence of Schneiderian first-rank symptoms such as thought insertion (though not fully endorsed), delusional perception, and third-person auditory hallucinations. No clear mood episodes were endorsed to support a schizoaffective or bipolar-related disorder.

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, my thoughts can get really loud or repetitive sometimes, and I can get stuck on something longer than I want to, but they still feel like they’re coming from me.

I don’t have the feeling that someone is putting a thought into my head like it wasn’t mine before, or reaching in and taking one out. It’s more like my own mind gets carried away, if that makes sense. Like I’ll overthink and circle around something, but I wouldn’t describe it as an outside force controlling it.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed thoughts being inserted or removed. At least not that I would recognize that way.
